items.title: UK's ASOS says cyber hack accessed customers' personal data
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: British online fashion retailer ASOS said on Thursday that a cybersecurity breach earlier this week had exposed some customers' personal information, including names and contact details, according to its initial investigation.
items.body:
British online fashion retailer ASOS (ASOS.L) said on Thursday that a [USN:L6N45S0OD TEXT:"cybersecurity breach"] earlier this week had exposed some customers' personal information, including names and contact details, according to its initial investigation.
It said the hacker also had access to "certain non-personal account related information," but no payment card information or account passwords, ASOS said in an email to customers.
"We discovered that an unauthorised party gained access to an ASOS employee account by impersonating a trusted contact to obtain log in credentials," ASOS said.
"Those credentials were then used to access information on certain third-party platforms used by ASOS."
It said the affected platforms were immediately locked down, ensuring that no further information could be accessed, adding that the ASOS website and app were safe to use throughout, and remain safe to use.
ASOS said it is working with the relevant law enforcement and regulatory authorities.
Shares in ASOS were up 3%, paring losses for the week to 8%.
So-called "social engineering" operations, where hackers impersonate workers to gain access to companies' computer networks, are prevalent.
British companies and institutions have been increasingly hit by aggressive and regular cyber and ransomware attacks in recent years. The British Library, a blood testing service, the London Underground, Marks & Spencer (MKS.L) , the Co-op and Jaguar Land Rover are some that have suffered months of disruption due to such breaches.

items.title: Kingspan hit with €40 million EU fine for misleading data on Slovenian deal
items.author: Yun Chee Foo
items.creator: Yun Chee Foo
items.summary: Irish building materials maker Kingspan was fined €40 million ($44.7 million) for providing incorrect and misleading information during an investigation into its abandoned acquisition of a Slovenian rival, EU antitrust regulators said on Thursday.
items.body:
Irish building materials maker Kingspan (KRX.I) was fined €40 million ($44.7 million) for providing incorrect and misleading information during an investigation into its abandoned acquisition of a Slovenian rival, EU antitrust regulators said on Thursday.
The sanction followed a four-year investigation by the European Commission, which is the European Union competition enforcer, and underscores its tough policy against such infringements of EU merger rules.
Kingspan said it would challenge the EU fine.
"We look forward to appealing the decision in full," the company said in an email.
EU antitrust chief Teresa Ribera said companies must adhere to merger rules.
"When companies withhold or distort the truth, they undermine a system that protects fair competition for everyone. There can be no compromise on disclosure and transparency. If they fail to do so, we do and will act firmly," she said in a statement.
Kingspan announced its plan to acquire Trimo in 2021 but scrapped the deal in April 2022 after the EU antitrust watchdog warned that the acquisition could jack up prices and reduce quality.
The Commission subsequently opened an investigation in November 2022 to examine whether Kingspan had provided incorrect and misleading information.
Its Thursday decision said the company provided misleading information about how it tracks penetration rates for mineral fibre sandwich panels and the availability of bidding data, as well as incorrect information about board members' involvement in certain matters.
Such breaches can cost companies fines up to 1% of their total global turnover.
($1 = 0.8940 euros)

items.title: Trump dismisses reports of potential strikes on Iran, says “productive discussions” ongoing, no attacks before midterms
items.summary: In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the blockade on Iranian maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz would remain in place while claiming that oil was continuing to flow in record volumes ...
items.body:
Trump dismisses reports of potential strikes on Iran, says “productive discussions” ongoing, no attacks before midterms In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the blockade on Iranian maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz would remain in place while claiming that oil was continuing to flow in record volumes through the strategic waterways with no Iranian oil involved. 
ANI | Updated: 08-10-2026 22:25 IST | Created: 08-10-2026 22:25 IST

US President Donald Trump (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump on Thursday dismissed reports of possible fresh strikes against Iran, saying “productive discussions” are underway with Tehran and making clear that the United States will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterm elections. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the blockade on Iranian maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz would remain in place while claiming that oil was continuing to flow in record volumes through the strategic waterways with no Iranian oil involved.
He also reiterated that Iran would not be allowed to possess a nuclear weapon. “We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran. I want to make it clear to everybody that, while Iran is in very bad condition, both Economically and Militarily, and while the Blockade will remain in full force and effect, with Oil flowing in Record Numbers of Barrels through the Hormuz Strait (22 Million Barrels, last night alone, with not one barrel coming from, or going to, Iran!), we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd. IRAN WILL NOT HAVE A NUCLEAR WEAPON!” the post read.
Trump's statement came a day after reports that the Pentagon had been instructed to prepare for a possible resumption of major combat operations against Iran, potentially ahead of the midterms. Axios report that Trump had not made a final decision on resuming major combat operations against Iran, but that the Pentagon had been instructed to prepare for possible fresh strikes.
According to Axios, citing US officials, the Pentagon instructed US Central Command several days ago to conclude preparations for resuming major combat operations in Iran. The directive did not set a specific date for any potential strikes. US and Israeli officials cited by the publication said renewed combat operations could take place before the US midterm elections, scheduled for November 3, and possibly ahead of Israeli elections expected a week earlier.
However, Trump's latest statement ruled out an attack before the US midterm elections while saying that discussions with Iran were continuing. Meanwhile, earlier in the day, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi said that Tehran would respond to a US peace proposal within the next few days, noting that the negotiations between Tehran and Washington remained ongoing and that messages were continuing to be exchanged through mediators.
“The negotiation process is still ongoing and messages are being exchanged through mediators,” Araghchi said, as quoted by Iranian state media Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB). The Iranian Foreign Minister said Tehran had already presented its proposal, referred to as the “Seven-Day Plan”, and had received the US side's views on it.
“We presented our plan, which we had presented under the title 'Seven-Day Plan', and we also heard the American side's views on it,” Araghchi said. “We are currently reviewing the views of the Americans and I think we will provide our response within the next few days,” he added.
The ongoing diplomatic exchanges are linked to Tehran's proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz under a seven-day plan, which Araghchi presented last month during the 81st United Nations General Assembly. Araghchi had said the timeline for the proposal would begin once the United States accepted it.
According to Al Jazeera, he said Washington would need to take certain actions under the plan, which could be completed within four to five days. “If they accept this plan tomorrow, the seven days will start from tomorrow,” Araghchi said.
He said the required steps were already part of a memorandum of understanding and would not be difficult to implement. Under the proposal, if the US fulfilled the conditions, the Strait of Hormuz could be reopened on the sixth day, followed by renewed talks between Tehran and Washington on the seventh day. Trump had earlier rejected the proposed arrangement, according to The Wall Street Journal. (ANI)

items.summary: Canada's main stock index clawed back some of the previous day's steep decline on Thursday as a jump in oil prices boosted energy shares.
items.body:
Canada's main stock index clawed back some of the previous day's steep decline on Thursday as a jump in oil prices boosted energy shares.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) ended up 103.52 points, or 0.3%, at 35,145.38, after on Wednesday falling 1.7% to its lowest closing level since July 20.
"People are reacting to the increased tensions in the Middle East," said Michael Sprung, president at Treegrove Investment Management.
"There's a lot to be concerned about in this environment," Sprung said, pointing to elevated oil prices and interest rates, as well as uncertainty around midterm elections in the United States.
Government borrowing costs globally have climbed in recent weeks on heightened worries about inflation and rising interest rates, along with nagging anxiety about nations' debt loads.
[USN:L1N45U031 TEXT:"US crude oil futures"] settled 3.6% higher at $91.49 a barrel on revived concerns about the ongoing war in the Middle East and growing supply disruptions due to a hurricane approaching the US Gulf Coast.
Energy (.SPTTEN) rose 2.8% and the materials group, which includes metal mining shares, ended 0.7% higher.
[USN:L1N45U0TG TEXT:"Gold"] rebounded from a two-month low as investors weighed the Federal Reserve's uncertain interest-rate path against growing concerns over high levels of US debt.
[USN:L1N45T0ZJ TEXT:"Richelieu Hardware"] (RCH.TO) was a standout. The hardware distributor's shares jumped 11.4% after the company reported increased third-quarter revenue.
Four of the 10 major sectors ended lower, including technology (.SPTTTK) . It lost 1.1% and heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) were down 0.3%.

items.title: Zelenskiy accuses US of inaction as Russian strikes kill over 70 in two days
items.author: Yuliia Dysa, Max Hunder
items.creator: Yuliia Dysa, Max Hunder
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy accused the US of being unwilling to help Ukraine after a Russian bomb attack on Thursday killed at least 35 people in the east, sending the two-day death toll from Russian strikes to over 70.
items.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy accused the US of being unwilling to help Ukraine after a Russian bomb attack on Thursday killed at least 35 people in the east, sending the two-day death toll from Russian strikes to over 70.
Hours after the strike on the embattled city of Kramatorsk tore through two buses, Zelenskiy criticised Washington's effort to pursue economic ties with Russia while also seeking to mediate the more than four-year war.
City authorities reported a new drone attack in the evening that killed two people. That brought to 35 the total death toll in the city.
Local authorities reported that a Russian guided aerial bomb killed two people in a village in southeastern Dnipropetrovsk and one person died in the western city of Ivano-Frankivsk.
The attacks were launched a day after a mass Russian drone and missile assault killed dozens across Ukraine — 22 of them in a residential building in the central town of Pryluky, around 130 km (80 miles) east of Kyiv.
Speaking in the early evening, Zelenskiy said 78 people were killed and 215 wounded by strikes in the last two days across Ukraine.
Speaking to reporters in Pryluky, the Ukrainian leader urged the US to accede to his requests to expand Ukraine's access to the Starlink satellite service to help it target Russian ballistic-missile launchers.
'THAT'S CALLED UNWILLINGNESS' "Open Starlink for Ukraine. You did open it when you were responding to Iran ... I’ve said quite openly — give it to us, help us defend our skies and dominate there. And then Putin will sit down at the negotiating table," he said in an emotional statement.
Ukraine has in recent months aimed to wrest the battlefield initiative from Russia, whose gains have slowed this year, but is still suffering from Moscow's increasingly brutal air war.
"So where's the truth here, where's the honesty? Where's the stalemate? ... That's called unwillingness," he said, referring to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's assertion earlier on Thursday the war is at [USN:L1N45U0GU TEXT:"a stalemate"] and that the United States would keep working toward a settlement.
"One cannot, on the one hand, negotiate with the Russians about future economic projects, whilst on the other hand say that we find ourselves in some sort of ... diplomatic stalemate," Zelenskiy added.
Top Russian and US officials, including US Special Envoy Jared Kushner, have [USN:L8N45G0SP TEXT:"held talks"] about bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream pipelines that delivered Russian gas to Germany before Moscow invaded Ukraine, Reuters reported on Thursday.
Ukrainian negotiators will travel to the US on Friday and Saturday for talks, Zelenskiy added, urging US President Donald Trump to increase sanction pressure on Russia.
Zelenskiy told reporters in Kyiv that he expected Kyiv's European partners to join the talks with the US. He also said Ukrainian negotiators would raise the issue of air defences in light of near-constant Russian attacks.
INTENSIFYING STRIKES Twenty people were wounded in the Kramatorsk strike — one of the biggest single attacks of the year by Russia. Moscow has denied targeting civilians, but regularly pounds cities with missiles and drones.
"The Russians are deliberately targeting civilians. For them, a bus full of passengers is an attractive target precisely because a single strike can kill as many people as possible," regional governor Vadym Filashkin said on the Telegram app.
Images posted by officials showed bodies strewn across a street littered with debris and a charred shell of a bus. Some bodies had not been identified yet, Zelenskiy said, adding that the attack would not go unanswered.
Separately, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said four people were killed and 19 wounded in morning attacks on the Ukrainian capital Kyiv. Water and electricity supplies were subject to interruptions which officials said would take time to put right.
Russia has unleashed relentless drone strikes against Kyiv in recent weeks, targeting warehouses, data centres and renewing its campaign against Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter.
Russian technology and AI company Yandex [USN:L8N45U1P7 TEXT:"said"] it could not yet determine whether equipment at a data centre hit by a Ukrainian drone attack could be restored. Zelenskiy did not refer specifically to the strike on Yandex, but said Ukraine was "mirroring" Russian attacks on data centres.

items.title: US suspends Permanent labour certification program for Infosys, Wipro, Tata, Microsoft and others, cites abuse of H1B program
items.summary: US Vice President JD Vance on Thursday announced the suspension of Microsoft from the Permanent Labor Certification program, alleging that the company had laid off American workers while benefiting ...
items.body:
US suspends Permanent labour certification program for Infosys, Wipro, Tata, Microsoft and others, cites abuse of H1B program US Vice President JD Vance on Thursday announced the suspension of Microsoft from the Permanent Labor Certification program, alleging that the company had laid off American workers while benefiting from thousands of H-1B visas and green cards.
ANI | Updated: 08-10-2026 21:29 IST | Created: 08-10-2026 21:29 IST

US VP JD Vance with Labour secretary Keith Sonderling and AG Todd Blanche on his left (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

In a far reaching move US Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling has announced that the US Government is suspending from the Permanent Labor Certification Program some of the largest IT outsourcing firms in the world which include Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, and Capgemini . The US Labour department attributed the suspension to multiple active federal investigations even as it also suspended US tech majors Microsoft and Adobe from the program. Speaking at a press conference on fighting visa fraud, US Vice President targeted the tech giants for alleged abuse of the H1B program
"The H1-B visa program is meant to allow companies to bring in really the best of the best from outside the United States of America for positions that are completely impossible to fill with American workers. Unfortunately, the program has become rife with fraud," he said Attorney General Todd Blanche said, "This announcement today should send and does send a strong signal to every single employer in the United States that the Trump Administration will not tolerate discrimination against American workers."
Vance further targeted tech giant Microsoft, alleging that the company had laid off American workers while benefiting from thousands of H-1B visas and green cards. Vance said Microsoft had laid off 6,000 American workers last year while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards.
"Microsoft laid off last year, 6000 American workers at the same time the company benefited from 6300 H-1B visas and almost 3000 green cards. If you do the math for every worker that Microsoft laid off they replace that worker with one and a half foreign indentured servants," he said. Vance said the administration's ongoing investigation had led to Microsoft's suspension from the programme.
"That's a scandalous system we've allowed in this country for far too long but thanks to the work of this task force and the empowerment of the President of the United States we are going to stop because thanks to an ongoing investigation we suspend the program for Microsoft which means they will no longer able to take those visas and apply for permanent status," he added He also said the Trump administration wanted companies operating in the US to expand while prioritising American workers.
"Our message to Microsoft in any other foreign or domestic corporation is simple. We want you to thrive in the United States of America. We want people to invest in the united states of America particularly the American technology sector, we are the biggest boosters of your industry. We want you to be able to grow and employ a lot of people but we want you to employ American workers. You are a great American company but you have to hire great American workers. You cannot lay off American workers and replace them with foreign indentured service," the US VP said. The US Labour secretary further said the department would not accept new applications or process pending permanent labor certification applications involving the companies.
"We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labor certification applications involving these companies," Sonderling said. Sonderling said the companies named had collectively sought millions of foreign workers and received hundreds of thousands of H-1B visa approvals and permanent labor certifications.
"Since 2009, just these companies alone have requested almost 3 million foreign workers. They received over 230,000 H1B Visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labor certifications that's hundred and thousands of jobs that were taken from a American workers," the Labor Secretary said. The announcement comes a day after the US Department of Homeland Security proposed new fees for F-1 nonimmigrant students seeking to participate in Optional Practical Training (OPT), describing the measure as an effort to protect American workers and strengthen the integrity of the immigration system.
Under the proposed rule announced on October 7, DHS would establish a USD 70,000 fee per F-1 nonimmigrant student for initial OPT and a USD 30,000 fee for any subsequent OPT. According to DHS, the proposal is aimed at reducing the flow of cheap labour into the United States, combating fraud and abuse, and making it easier for American citizens to compete in the job market.
"Optional Practical Training was never meant to be a back door into the American workforce, a subsidy for cheap labor, or a prize for those who game the system," a DHS spokesperson said. "DHS is upskilling OPT to require foreign students to justify their worth to employers. American workers should not have to compete against a program that has been turned into a pipeline for cheap foreign labor." Under existing federal regulations, eligible F-1 students can participate in OPT when the employment is directly related to their major area of study. Students require a recommendation from their designated school official and must apply for employment authorisation with US Citizenship and Immigration Services.
Eligible students can receive up to 12 months of OPT at each education level, while those who earn degrees in science, technology, engineering or mathematics fields may qualify for an additional 24-month extension. DHS said the proposed changes followed fraud and abuse identified by the Student and Exchange Visitor Program, including schemes involving problematic worksites and "pay-to-stay" visa arrangements.
The proposed fees would be paid by SEVP-certified schools before designated school officials recommend students for OPT in the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System and before students apply for employment authorisation with USCIS. DHS said the proposed fee would apply when schools recommend an F-1 student for any type of OPT and would not be tied to a particular employer. Collected fees would be deposited in the US Treasury.
The department will accept public comments on the proposed rule from October 8 through November 9, while the Paperwork Reduction Act section will have a separate 60-day public comment period. (ANI)

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [上海 ８日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は下落。１週間近くの国慶節の連休明けとなった中国本土の主要指数は、地政学...
items.body:
中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝下落、連休明けの中国は1年ぶり安値
10/8 17:48 配信

[上海 ８日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は下落。１週間近くの国慶節の連休明けとなった中国本土の主要指数は、地政学的緊張の再燃、世界的な利回り上昇で１年ぶりの安値を付けた。

中国の主要株価指数は現在、２年前の水準付近にある。当時は中国政府の大型景気刺激策が株価を押し上げ、緩やかな強気相場への期待が高まっていたが、足元では３カ月にわたり下落基調が続いている。

大型株で構成するＣＳＩ３００指数は１．１％安で終了。２０２５年８月以来の安値を付け、６月のピークから約１５％下落している。

上海総合指数は０．８％下落、ハイテク株中心の上海証券取引所の新興ハイテク企業向け市場「科創板」５０指数は５％近く急落し、５カ月ぶりの安値を付けた。

香港市場では、中国の連休中に２％近く下落したハンセン指数がこの日１．４％下落し、３カ月ぶりの安値を付けた。

上海卓鋳投資のパートナーは、上半期に半導体メーカーなどの「ハードテック」銘柄への過度な楽観が広がり、バリュエーションが不合理な水準まで押し上げられたと指摘。その上で、「バブルはいずれ必ず崩壊する」と述べた。

科創板５０指数は７月１日以降、時価総額の３分の１超を失ったが、株価収益率（ＰＥＲ）は依然として約１００倍となっている。

リスク選好度は、先月の首脳会談による楽観ムードが薄れ、米中間の緊張が再燃したことでも抑制された。

台湾の駐米大使に相当する人物は７日、先月のトランプ米大統領と習近平国家主席の首脳会談後も米国との関係は依然として強固だと述べた。

米連邦通信委員会（ＦＣＣ）は７日、中国の全ての試験機関が米国で使用される電子機器の試験を行うことを禁止する案を１０月２９日に採決すると発表した。これにより、これまでの中国を標的とした措置が拡大することになる。

トレーダーはまた、今月予定されている中国と欧州連合（ＥＵ）の通商協議にも注目している。中国はハイブリッド車輸出の自主規制というＥＵの要請を拒否したと伝えられている。

中信建投証券は、利回り格差の拡大が資本流出を誘発するため「米３０年債利回りの急速な上昇は中国株を引き続き抑制する」と指摘した。

８日の中国市場ではハイテク株が下げを主導し、半導体、バイオテクノロジー、ロボットの各指数はいずれも４％以上下落した。

一方、エネルギー、不動産、銀行は上昇、成長株から景気循環セクターに乗り換えが進んでいることを示した。

香港市場では、ハンセンテック指数が３％下落し、２年ぶりの安値を付けた。

items.title: French students keep up protest pressure with some demonstrations hit by violence
items.author: Manon Cruz, Dominique Vidalon
items.creator: Manon Cruz, Dominique Vidalon
items.summary: French teenagers blockaded some high schools and marched through cities on Thursday in the latest wave of nationwide protests about conditions in the country's schools, and some of the demonstrations were marred by violent unrest.
items.body:
French teenagers blockaded some high schools and marched through cities on Thursday in the latest wave of nationwide protests about conditions in the country's schools, and some of the demonstrations were marred by violent unrest.
The Interior Ministry said 71,500 people participated in the day's demonstrations, of which 24,500 took part in the main Paris protest centred around the Bastille square.
The Paris protest was mostly peaceful, although there were occasional clashes between small groups of demonstrators and the police during the evening.
Elsewhere, arsonists attacked a [USN:FWN45U1T1 TEXT:"Bordeaux"] police station, a school in Saint-Etienne was ransacked and a teacher in Toulouse was hit by a demonstrator, said the Interior Ministry.
In Marseille, police said a teacher at Victor Hugo High School [USN:FWN45U1T4 TEXT:"was attacked"] during the latest protests and has filed a criminal complaint over the incident.
Protesters clash with French gendarmes, as French high school and university students attend a demonstration, as part of a nationwide day of protests and blockades to demand better school conditions, in Nantes, France, October 8, 2026. REUTERS/Abdul Saboor Police use "flash-balls", as French high school and university students attend a demonstration, as part of a nationwide day of protests and blockades to demand better school conditions, in Nantes, France, October 8. REUTERS/Stephane Mahe Police officers in riot gear clash with demonstrators during nationwide protests in Paris, France, October 8, to demand better school conditions. REUTERS/Pedro Nunes People attend a demonstration at Place de la Bastille, during nationwide protests to demand better school conditions, in Paris, France, October 8. REUTERS/Pedro Nunes A police officer in riot gear uses a truncheon during nationwide protests in Paris, France, October 8, to demand better school conditions. REUTERS/Pedro Nunes Demonstrators gather on the July Column in Place de la Bastille during nationwide protests to demand better school conditions in Paris, France, October 8, . REUTERS/Pedro Nunes Protesters gather at Place de la Bastille during a demonstration by French high school and university students, as part of a nationwide day of protests and blockades supported by teachers and school parents to demand better school conditions, in Paris, France, October 8. REUTERS/Abdul Saboor French students gather outside the Lycee Henri-IV in Paris as part of nationwide protests to demand better school conditions in France, October 8. REUTERS/Abdul Saboor French high school students sit on barricades outside the Lycee Lamartine high school in Paris, as part of nationwide protests to demand better school conditions in France, October 8. REUTERS/Pedro Nunes Protesters march during a demonstration by French high school students, as part of a nationwide day of protests and blockades, expressing anger over overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages and dilapidated school buildings, which students blame on years of underinvestment, in Marseille, France, October 8. REUTERS/Manon Cruz A French high school student confronts people who want to prevent her from building a barricade, outside the Lycee Lamartine high school in Paris, as part of nationwide protests to demand better school conditions in France, October 8. REUTERS/Pedro Nunes Protesters face French CRS riot police outside Lycee Helene-Boucher high school as students block the road, during nationwide protests in Paris, France, October 8, to demand better school conditions. REUTERS/Pedro Nunes A person carries the French national flag as French high school and university students attend a demonstration, as part of a nationwide day of protests and blockades to demand better school conditions, in Nantes, France, October 8. REUTERS/Stephane Mahe People march during a demonstration by French high school students, as part of a nationwide day of protests and blockades, expressing anger over overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages and dilapidated school buildings, which students blame on years of underinvestment, in Marseille, France, October 8. A banner reads: "Funding cut, youth sacrificed." REUTERS/Manon Cruz The protest movement, now into its third week, has exposed deep tensions in France between popular demands for investments in deteriorating public services and a cash-strapped government under [USN:L8N45S1P0 TEXT:"pressure from bond markets"] to reduce its debt and deficit.
Protesters say they are demonstrating to demand more teachers and better facilities, arguing school buildings are often dilapidated, with overcrowded classrooms that are often freezing in winter and boiling in summer.
Critics say the movement has been infiltrated by violent far-left and anarchist elements.
High-school teacher Diane Di Sciullo joined students in Marseille, saying all they were asking for was a decent education in decent conditions. She denounced overcrowding, saying this year she had 37 students in her class.
"At the start of every lesson, I have to ask them to check the neighbouring classrooms for spare chairs and desks so they can actually study," she said.
Di Sciullo, 28, was carrying a placard that read, "I'm a teacher and my students help me catch cockroaches in class."
MINISTER PROMISES URGENT ACTION Education ministry figures showed the number of school blockades was gradually decreasing.
Education Minister Edouard Geffray told TF1 TV that extra teachers would be drafted in to plug gaps in schools which do not have enough teachers, while heavy school timetables will also be reviewed.
It is not uncommon for French teenagers to have lessons from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., as well as large amounts of homework.
Geffray also said he was working on potential improvements to Parcoursup, the national online portal for applying to university, which has been widely criticised as confusing and stressful for applicants.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu pledged late on Wednesday that the government would present "concrete, quick and fully funded responses" to the protests by late October, without offering specifics.
Student protest leaders said that was not good enough and called for further marches next Tuesday. There are also calls circulating online for a day of protests on October 17.
"Our demands must be heard. Yesterday, Mr Lecornu gave us a lot of hot air," said Ryad Rani, leader of one of the student unions.
"The mobilisation will continue, we're not backing down on anything."
A prominent complaint featured on banners and placards was that the police response to the wave of protests has been too heavy-handed. "Too young to be listened to, old enough to be tear-gassed" was one example.
There have been hundreds of arrests and dozens of injuries since the movement started. On Wednesday, the government [USN:L1N45T0EM TEXT:"suspended the use of stun grenades"] in the policing of the protests after one [USN:L1N45R08Q TEXT:"teenager's hand was blown off"].
POLITICAL RESPONSE SHOWS POLARISATION AS ELECTION LOOMS Six months from a presidential election, the protests have highlighted stark polarisation between leading candidates to replace Emmanuel Macron, who cannot seek a third term.
Far-right frontrunner Marine Le Pen has highlighted damage to schools caused by a minority of protesters and outlined [USN:L8N45R1J6 TEXT:"plans to slash public spending"] should she win.
Her hard-left opponent Jean-Luc Melenchon, who also has a chance of making the runoff, has praised the protesters as "incredible" and denounced police brutality.
According to an Elabe poll for BFM TV, 72% of French people think the students' demands are legitimate, but 55% of them think the protests should stop.
Neighbouring [USN:L1N45T0NH TEXT:"Belgium"] has also had student protests, with demonstrations in Brussels, Ciney and Liege.

items.title: ＦＲＢは追加利上げ必要、連続して行う必要なし＝ウォラー理事
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Howard Schneider

[ワシントン ８日 ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のウォラー理事は８日、...
items.body:
ＦＲＢは追加利上げ必要、連続して行う必要なし＝ウォラー理事
10/8 17:31 配信

写真は米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のウォラー理事。9月3日、ワシントンで撮影。REUTERS/Kylie Cooper

Howard Schneider

[ワシントン ８日 ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のウォラー理事は８日、インフレ率をＦＲＢの目標である２％まで引き下げるには、追加の利上げが必要になる可能性が高いと述べた。しかし、利上げのペースについては「柔軟性」があり、１０月２７─２８日の米連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で利上げをいったん見送る可能性も残した。

イスタンブールで開催されたトルコ中央銀行のフォーラムでの講演原稿によると、ウォラー氏は「経済データが予想通りに推移し続けるならば、インフレ率を目標の２％に早期に戻すために、追加利上げを実施すると予想している」と発言。

その上で「利上げの実施時期についてはある程度の柔軟性がある。利上げは連続した会合で実施する必要はなく、妥当な期間内に実施されるべきだ」と語った。

ウォラー氏の発言は、他のＦＲＢ当局者がここ数日に示した見解に重なるものであり、１０月のＦＯＭＣではフェデラルファンド（ＦＦ）金利誘導目標を現在の３．７５─４％に据え置く可能性が高いことを示唆している。１２月の利上げについては、新たな経済データが引き続き低い失業率と成長の継続を示す一方、インフレ抑制の進展が限定的あるいは全く見られない場合に行われる可能性があるとしている。

ＦＲＢは９月にＦＦ金利誘導目標を０．２５％ポイント引き上げたが、同時に発表された予測によると、ほとんどのＦＲＢ当局者は年末までにさらに０．２５％ポイントの利上げを予想している。

投資家は現在、ＦＲＢが１０月のＦＯＭＣ（米中間選挙のわずか１週間前）ではＦＦ金利を据え置くものの、その６週間後の１２月８─９日のＦＯＭＣでは利上げに踏み切ると見ている。

ウォラー氏は、現在ＦＲＢの目標を１％ポイント以上上回っているインフレ率を引き下げるために、ＦＦ金利をどれだけ追加で引き上げる必要があると考えているかについては言及しなかった。

同氏は、経済が回復し、イラン戦争によるエネルギー価格ショックが依然として解決されていないこと、そして人工知能（ＡＩ）の発展が主要な商品やサービスへの需要増加を通じてインフレを加速させているという新たな懸念があることから、金利引き上げの必要性が明確になったと説明した。

同氏は「今年後半に経済活動が強化されているという証拠があるため、金融引き締め政策が経済の深刻な減速を招く恐れがあるとは、それほど懸念していない」とした上で、「最近のインフレ加速は、消費者、投資家、そして価格決定権を持つ企業が将来のインフレ期待を上方修正するきっかけとなるのではないかと懸念している」と述べた。

ここ数日で、最終的に追加利上げの必要が生じる可能性を残しつつも、その前に様子を見る意向を示したＦＲＢ高官はウォラー氏で３人目。投資家はこのメッセージを、次回のＦＯＭＣへの期待値を設定する際に考慮に入れているようだ。

ＦＲＢ議長に就任する際、今後の政策決定について多くを語ることを避けたいと述べていたウォーシュ氏は、何もコメントしていない。

だが、ウォラー氏らは議論を続けている。ウォラー氏は８日の発言の中で、他のＦＲＢ高官らの最近の発言が特定の成果を約束することなく、金利の推移に関する市場の確率設定にどのように役立ったかを説明した。これは、投資家が全くシグナルを受け取れない場合に起こりうる変動を回避できる、より良い政策決定手法だと主張した。

同氏は、政策立案者は「最終的な目的地が決まっていないことを認めつつ、今後どのような方向に向かう可能性が高いかを示すことができる」と述べ、「このシグナルは短期金利の方向性を定めるのに役立つ一方で、今後のデータに基づいて利上げを調整する柔軟性も提供する」と語った。

ウォラー氏は、ＦＲＢの政策に関する情報発信を完全に停止することは賢明ではないと主張している。

Ericsson CEO for South-East Asia, Oceania and India Andres Vicente said India’s rapid 5G adoption and investment in advanced networks have created a strong foundation for the next stage of digital growth. He said the transition to 5G Standalone would make networks more programmable and support differentiated connectivity, new AI-powered use cases and the eventual evolution towards 6G.
GSMA Director General Vivek Badrinath said the focus is shifting from simply connecting people to determining what more than a billion connected people and businesses can do with digital infrastructure. “AI will be a major part of what comes next,” he said, stressing the importance of compute, models, data and skills alongside more intelligent and programmable networks. Qualcomm ISAG Chair Etienne Chaponniere highlighted another major shift, saying AI could become the new user interface as devices increasingly understand their surroundings and process information locally. He said greater on-device processing would reduce the need to send all data back to networks and have implications for the design and standardisation of future networks.
TIM Head of European Affairs and Economic Studies Giacomo Robustelli said AI should also be viewed as an infrastructure revolution, with every new AI application increasing demand for connectivity, computing, storage and security. On 6G, Bharat 6G Alliance Chairman N.G. Subramaniam said the technology would go beyond faster speeds to make networks more intelligent, with communications and AI evolving together. He said India’s 6G development is being pursued in mission mode with government support and industry participation in research and innovation.
C-DOT CEO Rajkumar Upadhyay meanwhile called for India’s telecom manufacturing ecosystem to move beyond production towards greater value creation through design, intellectual property and domestically developed equipment, alongside increased investment in security, quality, AI and cybersecurity. items.body:
ＥＣＢ最低準備率引き上げに反対、信頼低下招く＝ベルギー中銀総裁
10/8 17:12 配信

写真は欧州中央銀行（ECB）本部の看板。2018年4月、フランクフルトで撮影。REUTERS/Kai Pfaffenbach

[フランクフルト ８日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）理事会メンバーのウンシュ・ベルギー中央銀行総裁は、民間銀行に義務付ける法定準備預金の比率を引き上げる案に反対した。将来の政策運営に対する信頼を損ない、財政政策の領域に踏み込む恐れもあると警告した。

ＥＣＢ内では現在、銀行が無利子で預け入れる法定準備預金の割合を引き上げるべきかどうかが議論されている。ＥＣＢ自身の損失を減らすとともに、高インフレ下で金融環境を一段と引き締める狙いがある。

ウンシュ氏はブリュッセルでの会議で「（法定準備預金の）最低準備率引き上げについて、現在議論が進んでいる。もちろん引き続き利息を付けないという前提だ」と説明。「率直に言って、その理屈は私にはあまり明確ではなく、説得力があるとも思えない」と述べた。

ＥＣＢは新型コロナ禍前の金利がゼロ以下だった時期に、債券買い入れを通じて数兆ユーロの余剰流動性を生み出した。現在は商業銀行がこの資金をＥＣＢに預け入れ、ＥＣＢは多額の利払いを強いられている。このため中央銀行の損失が膨らんでいる。

ウンシュ氏は「損失を抑えることが目的なら、最低準備率は財政政策に近い手段になる」と指摘。「通常、財政政策は中央銀行に与えられた役割ではない」と述べた。

また、こうした措置で銀行の利子収入が減れば、将来の債券買い入れ策への参加に銀行が消極的になる恐れがあり、中央銀行の政策運営に対する信頼を損ないかねないと述べた。

items.title: Imran Khan’s son says “no update” on “abducted” sisters of former PM; no contact with father for six months
items.summary: The three sisters were detained for 30 days ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI)'s planned protest march to Islamabad last month demanding updates on Khan's health as well as his release from ...
items.body:
Imran Khan’s son says “no update” on “abducted” sisters of former PM; no contact with father for six months The three sisters were detained for 30 days ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI)'s planned protest march to Islamabad last month demanding updates on Khan's health as well as his release from Adiala Jail, where the PTI founder has been incarcerated since August 2023.
ANI | Updated: 08-10-2026 20:12 IST | Created: 08-10-2026 20:12 IST

Noreen Niazi (Left), Aleema Khanum (Centre) and Uzma Khanum, sisters of jailed former Prime Minister of Pakistan and founder of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party Imran Khan (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan’s son Kasim Khan on Thursday claimed that his three aunts remain “abducted” by the Pakistani authorities and that their family and lawyers have received no update about their condition or the reasons for their incarceration, while noting that he and his brother have had no contact with their father for more than six months. The three sisters were detained for 30 days ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI)'s planned protest march to Islamabad last month demanding updates on Khan's health as well as his release from Adiala Jail, where the PTI founder has been incarcerated since August 2023.
In a post on X, Kasim Khan linked the situation of his aunts with the continued lack of contact with his father, saying that he and his brother have not spoken to Imran Khan for more than six months. "Currently, my Aunties are still abducted. Family and lawyers have received no update on how they are, nor why they are incarcerated. Concerning my father, there is complete silence. My brother and I have had no contact with him for more than six months. We do not even know the true state of his health," the post read.
He also referred to protests in Pakistan over the former prime minister's imprisonment, noting that the people were continuing to demand justice and the right to be heard. "Meanwhile, thousands of Pakistanis are peacefully taking to the streets to protest against his illegal and politically motivated imprisonment. However, the people of Pakistan have not given up. No barricade, intimidation or repression can muzzle the people’s demand for justice and their democratic right to be heard. There can be no lasting peace or stability while their democratic will is suppressed and their chosen leader remains behind bars,” Kasim Khan added.
His remarks come a day after the families of Khan’s detained sisters, Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan, approached the Lahore High Court, seeking permission for family members and lawyers to meet them. According to Dawn, Advocate Rana Mudassar Umar filed two separate civil miscellaneous applications in the pending writ petitions on the matter on behalf of Shah Raiz Khan, son of Aleema Khan, and Sakeena Niazi, daughter of Noreen Niazi.
The pleas challenged the denial of meetings between the three sisters and their family members and lawyers, as well as access to medicines. The families have alleged that neither relatives nor legal counsel have been allowed to meet the detained women or provide them with medicines.
The applications stated that medicines had been provided to the sisters on only one occasion and that no one had subsequently been allowed to meet them, Dawn reported. The pleas have raised concerns over the health of the detained sisters and sought directions from the Lahore High Court allowing their lawyers and family members to meet them and provide medicines, as reported by Dawn.
Imran Khan's sisters were detained for 30 days ahead of the party's September 27 protest call. The detentions came amid reports of a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its September 27 countrywide protest and march to Islamabad.
The party had called for the demonstrations to demand Imran Khan's release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. On September 24, the Lahore High Court had declined a request to immediately suspend the notifications for the preventive detention of the sisters. (ANI)

items.title: 国内大手金融5社トップ、金利上昇を前向き評価　財政懸念も指摘
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Miho Uranaka

[東京 ８日 ロイター] - 三井住友フィナンシャルグループ（ＳＭＦＧ）などの大手金融機関５...
items.body:
国内大手金融5社トップ、金利上昇を前向き評価　財政懸念も指摘
10/8 16:41 配信

日本のメガバンクの看板。2018年4月3日、都内で撮影。 REUTERS/Toru Hanai
現在値 三菱ＵＦＪ 3,477 -27
Miho Uranaka

[東京 ８日 ロイター] - 三井住友フィナンシャルグループ（ＳＭＦＧ）などの大手金融機関５社のトップは８日、日本経済新聞社主催のシンポジウムに出席し、国内の金利上昇について、企業の設備投資や経済成長を反映した動きだとして前向きな評価を示した。ただ、財政懸念などによる「悪い金利上昇というような要素も入っている」（ＳＭＦＧ中島達社長）との指摘もあった。株式市場については強気な見方が多かった。

三菱ＵＦＪフィナンシャル・グループ ＜ 8306.T ＞ の半沢淳一社長は、日本経済は長年のデフレ状態から「物価、賃金、経済活動がある意味正常化する局面」にまで進んだと指摘。「経済の実力や物価上昇率の高まりに見合った金利上昇であれば、経済正常化の一環として前向きに捉えるべきだ」と述べた。一方、物価上昇や日銀の利上げ観測に加え、財政の持続可能性に対する市場の見方を背景としたリスクプレミアムの上昇も一部反映されているとの認識を示した。

中島氏も現在の金利上昇について「概ね良い金利上昇の結果」と評価。同時に、「日本の財政が将来にわたって、しっかり健全性が維持されるのかと懸念を抱いている投資家も、やはり一定はいる」と述べた。財政懸念に加え、中東情勢を巡るリスクも一部金利に織り込まれているという。

今後のリスクとして、みずほフィナンシャルグループの木原正裕社長は、各国政府の財政拡張や人工知能（ＡＩ）・データセンター分野を中心とした旺盛な投資需要を背景に長期資金の獲得競争が起きていることを挙げた。「長期金利が高騰しやすい環境」とみて、低格付け企業への影響を注視しているという。中東情勢の悪化による原油調達コスト上昇の影響も、国内経済にとって「非常に心配だ」と述べた。

中島氏は、米国を中心とするＡＩ向けデータセンター投資について、「将来しっかりキャッシュフローを生むのか若干疑問を呈する投資家も出てきている」と指摘。その上で、「投資がスローダウンするようなことがあれば、世界経済に相当大きなインパクトをもたらす」と警戒感を示した。ただ、国内企業の資金需要は依然として強いという。

株式市場の先行きについては、総じて強気な見方が多い。野村ホールディングスの奥田健太郎社長は好調な企業業績やガバナンス改革を背景に「海外投資家の日本株への関心は高い」と指摘し、日経平均は年末にかけて７万５０００円前後、２０２７年末には８万円超も視野に入ると見込む。

大和証券グループ本社の荻野明彦社長はさらに強気で、年末８万円、２７年末に８万８０００円に達する可能性があると予想。日本株の評価見直しは中長期的に続くとの見方から、２０４５年には３０万円に到達する可能性にも言及した。ただ、地政学や金融政策を巡る不確実性そのものよりも、「市場のボラティリティーが過度に上昇することが一番のリスク」という。

items.body:
アジア株式市場サマリー：引け（8日）
10/8 16:17 配信

豪証券取引所のロゴ。2018年2月8日、シドニーで撮影。REUTERS/Daniel Munoz

インド株式市場は続落して引けた。ＳＥＮＳＥＸ指数が３２カ月ぶり安値に沈んだ。原油価格の高騰、世界的な国債利回り上昇、ルピー安を背景にインフレ懸念が強まった。前日は中央銀行によるタカ派的利上げに圧迫されていた。

ＮＳＥ指数は１．６４％安の２万２２３１．８、ＳＥＮＳＥＸ指数は１．４４％安の７万１５９３．２４で終了。ＮＳＥ指数は１８カ月ぶりの安値で引けた。

外国人投資家の売りが加速、過去９日間では４６９９億ルピー（４８億６０００万ドル）を売り越した。年初来の資金流出は過去最大の３０４億ドルに達した。

ＮＳＥ指数とＳＥＮＳＥＸ指数は先週に一時持ち直したものの、再び売られ過ぎの水準に戻った。相対力指数（ＲＳＩ）は３０を下回り、売り圧力の強さを示している。

主要１６業種は全て下落。小型株指数は２．３％、中型株指数は２．５％それぞれ下げた。

中国・香港株式市場は下落。１週間近くの国慶節の連休明けとなった中国本土の主要指数は、地政学的緊張の再燃、世界的な利回り上昇で１年ぶりの安値を付けた。

中国の主要株価指数は現在、２年前の水準付近にある。当時は中国政府の大型景気刺激策が株価を押し上げ、緩やかな強気相場への期待が高まっていたが、足元では３カ月にわたり下落基調が続いている。

大型株で構成するＣＳＩ３００指数は１．１％安で終了。２０２５年８月以来の安値を付け、６月のピークから約１５％下落している。

上海総合指数は０．８％下落、ハイテク株中心の上海証券取引所の新興ハイテク企業向け市場「科創板」５０指数は５％近く急落し、５カ月ぶりの安値を付けた。

香港市場では、中国の連休中に２％近く下落したハンセン指数がこの日１．４％下落し、３カ月ぶりの安値を付けた。

上海卓鋳投資のパートナーは、上半期に半導体メーカーなどの「ハードテック」銘柄への過度な楽観が広がり、バリュエーションが不合理な水準まで押し上げられたと指摘。その上で、「バブルはいずれ必ず崩壊する」と述べた。

科創板５０指数は７月１日以降、時価総額の３分の１超を失ったが、株価収益率（ＰＥＲ）は依然として約１００倍となっている。

リスク選好度は、先月の首脳会談による楽観ムードが薄れ、米中間の緊張が再燃したことでも抑制された。

台北駐米経済文化代表処代表（駐米大使に相当）は７日、先月のトランプ米大統領と習近平国家主席の首脳会談後も米国との関係は依然として強固だと述べた。

米連邦通信委員会（ＦＣＣ）は７日、中国の全ての試験機関が米国で使用される電子機器の試験を行うことを禁止する案を１０月２９日に採決すると発表した。これにより、これまでの中国を標的とした措置が拡大することになる。

トレーダーはまた、今月予定されている中国と欧州連合（ＥＵ）の通商協議にも注目している。中国はハイブリッド車輸出の自主規制というＥＵの要請を拒否したと伝えられている。

中信建投証券は、利回り格差の拡大が資本流出を誘発するため「米３０年債利回りの急速な上昇は中国株を引き続き抑制する」と指摘した。

８日の中国市場ではハイテク株が下げを主導し、半導体、バイオテクノロジー、ロボットの各指数はいずれも４％以上下落した。

一方、エネルギー、不動産、銀行は上昇、成長株から景気循環セクターに乗り換えが進んでいることを示した。

香港市場では、ハンセンテック指数が３％下落し、２年ぶりの安値を付けた。

ソウル株式市場は下落して引けた。半導体株の軟調に加え、原油高を背景としたインフレ懸念が重しとなり２週連続で下落となった。

総合株価指数（ＫＯＳＰＩ）は週間では５．７９％下落した。

半導体大手サムスン電子は２．４２％、同業のＳＫハイニックスは２．４４％それぞれ下落した。

海外での起債がブームとなるなか韓国企画財政部当局者はロイターに対し、国内の証券業ライセンスを持たない投資銀行が韓国企業の国外債発行を主幹事として引き受けることを禁止する案を検討していると明らかにした。

サムスン電子は、人工知能（ＡＩ）向け半導体の需要急拡大がメモリー販売の好調を支えたとして、第３・四半期の利益がほぼ９倍に跳ね上がり、四半期営業利益がテクノロジー企業として世界初の水準となる１００兆ウォン（７４７億５０００万ドル）を突破する見通しだと公表した。

国際エネルギー機関（ＩＥＡ）は、以前に発表された石油放出をできる限り速やかに完了させれば、市場に約１億バレルを供給できると表明した。ただし、アナリストや一部の政府は、この数字が必ずしも同規模の新たな介入を意味するわけではないと指摘した。

外国人投資家は１兆９８８５億ウォンの売り越しだった。

ＫＯＳＰＩの年初来上昇率は５７．２３％となっている。

シドニー株式市場は反落して引けた。鉱業株が下げを主導した。鉄鉱石大手フォーテスキューが手元資金の減少を警告、業績見通しは中国鉱産資源集団（ＣＭＲＧ）との交渉次第と表明したことが響いた。

Ｓ＆Ｐ／ＡＳＸ２００指数は１週間ぶりの大幅安となった。

世界第４位の鉄鉱石採掘会社フォーテスキューの株価は一時４．２％下落し、１年超ぶりの安値を付けた。第１・四半期の出荷量が減少したものの、ＣＭＲＧとの交渉次第という条件付きで２０２７年度のガイダンスは据え置いた。また７－９月四半期に手元資金が３７％減少し、純有利子負債が６月３０日時点の９億ドルから２８億ドルへと３倍超に膨らんだと明らかにした。

バレンジョイの鉱業調査責任者グリン・ロウコック氏は、ＢＨＰがＣＭＲＧとの同様の紛争をすでに解決していることを指摘、フォーテスキューが現時点でより直接的な影響を受けていると述べた。その上で、ギニアのシマンドゥ鉱山プロジェクトからの供給増加で主導権が買い手側に移るのに伴い、年次交渉は全ての生産者にとってより厳しくなると警告した。

同氏はさらに、鉄鉱石は長年にわたり豪税収やロイヤルティー収入の重要な源泉となってきたため、この問題は政府歳入の減少にもつながり得ると述べた。

フォーテスキューの下落を受け、鉱業株指数は２％下落した。同業のリオ・ティントとＢＨＰはそれぞれ２．９％、２％下落した。

金融株指数は１％安と続落。四大銀行は１．５─１．６％下落した。

ハイテク株指数は、米ナスダック総合指数に連れて０．８％下落した。ヘルスケア株指数は０．１％下落した。

一方、エネルギー株指数は２週間ぶりの高値を付けた。原油価格が上昇し１バレル＝１００ドルをわずかに上回ったことが追い風となった。

ウッドサイド・エナジーは２．６％上昇した。

items.body:
セブン＆アイ、3－8月の純利益は2.2％増　国内減益も「挽回の余地」
10/8 16:12 配信

セブン＆アイ・ホールディングスのロゴ。２０１７年１２月、都内で撮影。REUTERS/Toru Hanai

Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ８日 ロイター] - セブン＆アイ・ホールディングスが８日発表した２０２７年２月期中間期（２６年３－８月）の連結純利益は前年比２．２％増の１２４４億円だった。海外コンビニ事業が好調だった。国内は減益だったが、下期に「挽回の余地」があるとしている。

同社は昨年、ヨーク・ホールディングスやセブン銀行を連結対象から切り離しており、この影響を調整した実質ベースの純利益は、前年比１７．８％増だった。

国内コンビニ事業では、営業利益が前年比９．８％減の１０９８億円となった。店内調理設備や次世代店舗システムの導入の先行投資に加え、物価上昇などで販管費が増加した。「セブンカフェ ベーカリー」などの取り組みを進め、客単価は上昇、既存店売り上げは前年同期を上回った。

海外コンビニ事業は、営業利益が同８７．７％増の１５０４億円だった。ドルベースの米国内既存店商品売り上げは前年同期を上回った。ガソリンについても市況変動の影響で収益が前年同期を上回った。ただ、６－８月期はガソリン価格が高い水準で推移したことを含む厳しい外部環境で客数は減少し、米既存店商品売り上げは前年同期をやや下回った。

通期純利益については、同５％減の２７８０億円とした従来予想を維持した。ＩＢＥＳがまとめたアナリスト１６人の純利益予想の平均値２７７８億円と同水準だった。

セブン―イレブン・ジャパンの阿久津知洋社長は決算会見で、夏場の季節要因が影響したとし「少し悪くなった時に、それを跳ね返すだけの実力が身についていないと改めて感じた」と話した。その上で「通期の目標を維持したのは、この後まだまだ挽回の余地があるからだ」と語り、玩具などエンタメに関わる商材が伸びるとの見通しを語った。

スティーブン・ヘイズ・デイカス最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は、将来を見据えると、日本と北米以外の地域で「第３の柱」が必要になると語り、今から準備するためのリソースや人材を整えていると話した。 

＜下期からＰａｙＰａｙ、ＬＩＮＥ活用し販促＞

セブン＆アイは７月、ソフトバンクやＰａｙＰａｙ、三井住友カードから総額３０００億円の出資を受ける戦略的パートナーシップを発表している。高木哲也ＣＦＯ（最高財務責任者）は「下期から早速、各社と販促策を予定している」と説明。ＰａｙＰａｙや、パートナーシップに加わるＬＩＮＥヤフーのＬＩＮＥを通じてクーポンを活用する策など「これまでセブン―イレブンを利用いただけていない顧客を誘引する取り組みを予定している」と話した。

来期には顧客ＩＤの統合を進め、ストアポイントの導入などでセブン―イレブンへの送客効果の拡大を期待しており「リテールメディアとの融合も視野に、テクノロジーの活用による革新的な顧客体験の提供を実現する取り組み」になると話した。中長期的にはＡＩ（人工知能）ロボティックスの活用も視野に入れているという。

ミニストップ、27年2月期50億円の最終赤字に　店内加工食品の販売下振れ
10/8 16:10 配信

[東京 ８日 ロイター] - ミニストップは８日、２０２７年２月期の連結業績が５０億円の最終赤字（前年実績５６億円の赤字）になりそうだと発表した。１億円の黒字を見込んでいたが、手作りおにぎりなどの販売減少を補うために強化した店内加工食品が、品ぞろえの遅れや天候不順で計画を下回った。保有する店舗など固定資産の減損損失８億円を計上したことも響く。

items.author: ロイター

items.body:
日経平均は続落、利益確定売り　金利先高観も重し
10/8 16:08 配信

東京証券取引所。都内で２０２０年１０月撮影。REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon

Hiroko Hamada

[東京 ８日 ロイター] - 東京株式市場で日経平均は続落し、前営業日比１．４２％（９９３円６０銭）安の６万９０４２円１１銭で取引を終えた。指数寄与度の大きいＡＩ（人工知能）・半導体関連株を中心に利益確定売りが出たほか、金利の先高観が重しとなり、幅広い銘柄が値下がりした。日経平均は安値引けとなった。

日経平均は小幅安でスタートした後、次第に下げ幅を拡大。前日の米株安の流れを引き継ぐ形となった。韓国サムスン電子の好決算を受けて、前場中盤は下げ渋ったが、後場に入ると再び売りが強まった。ＡＩ関連株のほか、機械株や銀行株の下げが目立った。

後場後半には、半導体受託製造世界最大手の台湾積体電路製造（ＴＳＭＣ）の第３・四半期の売上高が過去最高の１兆４９００億台湾ドル（４６７億１０００万米ドル）に達したと伝わったが、相場の反応は限られた。

市場では、金利の先高観が株価の上値を抑制しているとの見方もあった。フランスの財政懸念を背景に金利が急上昇し、「世界的に長期金利を中心に上昇圧力が強まるとの懸念が相場の重しとなっている」（国内証券・ストラテジスト）との声が聞かれた。

いちよし証券の投資情報部・銘柄情報課課長、及川敬司氏は「ＡＩ関連株に関しては、６月にかけての急騰後の調整を見た後なので、上がったところでは利益確定売りを出したいという投資家も多いのではないか」と話している。

日経平均は目先、７万円前後で推移すると予想され、「企業決算が本格化するタイミングでは上方向を試す動きとなりそうだ」（及川氏）という。

ＴＯＰＩＸは１．５１％安の４０９１．４６ポイントで取引を終えた。東証プライム市場指数は前営業日比１．５１％安の２１０９．４８ポイントだった。プライム市場の売買代金は７兆６１３３億９３００万円だった。東証３３業種では、海運、サービス、ゴム製品など７業種が値上がり。非鉄金属、ガラス・土石製品、銀行など２６業種は値下がりした。

新興株式市場では、東証グロース市場２５０指数が続落し、２．２９％安の７９４．７５ポイントだった。

個別では、ソフトバンクグループ、東京エレクトロン、フジクラ、ＴＤＫが軟調。一方、リクルートホールディングス、トレンドマイクロは上昇。前日に決算を発表したツルハホールディングスもしっかりだった。キオクシアホールディングスは買われていたが、終値では前日比横ばい。

東証プライム市場の騰落数は、値上がりが３２７銘柄（２１％）、値下がりは１１８２銘柄（７６％）、変わらずは４３銘柄（２％）だった。

items.title: Britain says consulate in Jerusalem to remain open as a UK Mission
items.author: CNA
items.summary: Israel ordered the British consulate in East Jerusalem to close after London announced plans to impose sanctions on settlements in the West Bank.
items.body:

Britain says consulate in Jerusalem to remain open as a UK Mission

Israel ordered the British consulate in East Jerusalem to close after London announced plans to impose sanctions on settlements in the West Bank.

The exterior of the British consulate on the deadline set by Israel for its closure, following trade sanctions imposed by British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, in East Jerusalem, October 8, 2026. REUTERS/Ammar Awad

FAST

LONDON: Britain and Israel announced on Thursday (Oct 8) that the nearly 200-year-old British diplomatic mission in Jerusalem would stay open at a smaller scale and with a new name, in a compromise after Israel ordered the consulate shut in a sanctions dispute.

Under the last-minute agreement, Britain will rename the consulate, founded in 1839, as the "UK Mission" in the city.

Israel said 20 British diplomats including the consul general would depart, leaving just seven working at the mission in a limited role. Britain said it had withdrawn some diplomats "temporarily", intended to build back its presence, and would hold off on reciprocal measures for now.

The agreement appeared to ward off a major diplomatic crisis between longstanding allies. In recent days, sources had said Britain had been prepared to consider ejecting Israeli diplomats if the mission were closed.

Israel had issued a 30-day deadline last month for Britain to close the consulate , after London announced sanctions targeting Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank , including a ban on trade in goods from there.

In a statement, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said the consulate would formally end operations but that some British diplomats would be allowed to continue working there.

Saar's British counterpart, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, said his country does not accept that Israel has the legal right to close the consulate. The consulate is in a part of the city Israel captured in a 1967 war, which Israel later annexed in a move that most countries do not recognise.

Following discussions with Israel, "our Consulate General building will not be closing, and will be known as the UK Mission, Jerusalem from today," Miliband said. It would continue to "deliver vital services and our work with the Palestinian people."

A car enters the British Consulate after the sign outside the consulate was taken down in East Jerusalem on Oct 8, 2026. (File Photo: AP/Mahmoud Illean)

WORKERS REMOVE SIGNAGE FROM CONSULATE BUILDING On Thursday morning workers in the consulate removed a plaque reading "British Consulate General" and another sign for its consular section. The British flag was still flying over the building.

Saar said that Israel and Britain had reached an understanding on Wednesday night to prevent a further deterioration in relations between the two countries, and that Britain had agreed not to take any measures in retaliation.

Miliband said Britain had "temporarily withdrawn a number of staff and families to ensure their safety and security" and that it would work in the coming months to build back its presence.

"We will not take reciprocal action while such discussions are underway and credible," Miliband said in a statement.

Last week, Britain's top national security adviser Jonathan Powell visited Israel in a bid to keep the consulate from closing.

Britain's minister for the Middle East, Stephen Doughty, told Sky News that Britain was engaged in ongoing talks with the Israeli government, and that it deeply regretted Israel's actions in relation to its consulate.

"Our building remains open, our staff remain doing important work," Stephen Doughty told Sky News. "We retain a presence in Jerusalem ... and it is very important that work is able to continue."

The closure order does not affect Britain's embassy in Tel Aviv, which handles diplomatic relations with Israel's government.

The consulate, in the Sheikh Jarrah neighbourhood of East Jerusalem, has handled Britain's relations with Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza, andprovided consular services to Palestinians.

The British sanctions announcement, and Israel's order to close the consulate, mark a new low in a relationship that has deteriorated over the past three years. Britain has repeatedly criticised Israel over its actions in the war in Gaza and over Israeli settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government, which faces an election later this month, has accused Britain's governing Labour Party of being hostile towards Israel.

items.title: Indian firms seen posting faster profit growth despite global headwinds
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: Indian companies are projected to achieve profit growth during the September quarter despite various challenges affecting different sectors. Foreign investors are retreating from Indian stocks, impacting the benchmark Nifty 50 index's performance this year. Strong domestic demand and favorable conditions in certain sectors are expected to sustain earnings growth for many firms. Analysts believe that financials will be a significant driver of earnings, supported by healthy loan growth.
items.body: Indian companies' September-quarter profit growth is expected to accelerate even as performance is likely to be uneven across sectors due to global and local headwinds, according to five brokerages.Foreign investors have pulled out of Indian stocks at a record pace, pushing the benchmark Nifty 50 towards its worst year in 15 years. While a weakest-in-a-decade monsoon has raised rural demand concerns, the Middle East conflict has fuelled inflation concerns globally, raising the risk premium on emerging market economies and equity markets.However, resilient domestic demand in Q2, early festive inventory build-up, favourable pricing in selective commodity-linked sectors should continue to support earnings growth, said J.P.Morgan analysts led by Rajiv Batra.Nifty 50 firms' net profit is forecast to rise about 20% year-on-year on average, based on brokerage estimates. In April-June, it hit a 10-quarter high of 18% following three quarters of low-single-digit growth.Motilal Oswal is the most optimistic, forecasting a 27% increase in net profit, which would be the fastest in 17 quarters.The broker is bullish on automobiles and new-age tech platforms, picking the likes of Meesho, PhysicsWallah, Mahindra & Mahindra and TVS Motor, on structural growth trends, recovering discretionary demand and expanding product portfolios.PhillipCapital expects a modest 13% rise, reflecting margin pressure and a less favourable mix outside the oil and gas sector.Tata Consultancy Services will kickstart the earnings season on Friday.Sector WatchMost analysts back financials to be the principal earnings anchor, with healthy loan growth, lower credit costs and fewer loans turning bad at banks. Following the Reserve Bank of India's rate hike and its shift to a 'calibrated tightening' stance, we expect large private banks to see further earnings upgrades, said J.P.Morgan.Multiple brokerages say earnings from ICICI Bank, State Bank of India and Bajaj Finance would stand out.Effects of the US-Iran war, now in its eighth month, are likely to be felt sharply across automobiles, energy and consumer goods, as oil from the region struggled to get through to India, the world's third-largest crude importer, raising costs.Automobile retail sales rose during the quarter on improved product mix, pricing and tax cuts.However, Kotak Institutional Equities expects commodity headwinds to drag operating margins.Higher crude prices are likely to favour upstream and oil-to-chemicals companies, while pressuring oil marketing firms.Oil-to-telecom conglomerate and operator of the world's largest refining complex, Reliance Industries, is expected to benefit from this, tiding over a relatively softer retail performance.IT demand may remain subdued as clients delay non-essential spending amid AI-driven pricing pressure. We expect management commentaries to reflect the multi-pronged challenges the sector faces - geopolitics, weak macro and AI threat, Nuvama said.

3 killed, dozens injured in Houthi attacks on two Saudi airports

King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh & Abha airport came under fire. Eighty-two military targets were destroyed in retaliation, Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said.

Sherif Tarek

08 October, 2026 12:11 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

An air traffic control tower at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Photographer: AFP/Getty Images/ Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-
A+

-->

The Iran-backed Houthis struck two airports in Saudi Arabia, killing three people and injuring dozens as the militant group intensifies its attacks on the kingdom while fighting Saudi-backed forces in Yemen.

King Khalid International Airport in the capital, Riyadh, and Abha airport in the southwestern region came under fire on Tuesday and Wednesday, with the two strikes causing damage, the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation said in a statement. The Houthis claimed to have attacked both airports.

A Sudanese man was killed in the assault on the Riyadh airport, according to GACA. Five Saudi nationals, two Egyptians and a Pakistani resident were injured.

Show Full Article

Two women, one Moroccan and one Algerian, were killed in the strike on Abha International Airport, where 28 people, including Saudi citizens, sustained injuries ranging from minor to serious.

GACA said it was working to “assess the damage, verify the safety of the facilities and take the necessary measures to ensure the safety of passengers and maintain the security and safety of operations within the Kingdom’s civil aviation system.”

In retaliation, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said it had destroyed 82 military targets belonging to the Houthis in Saada, Hodeida, Jawf and Marib. These included ballistic missile storage sites and command and control centers, a spokesman for the coalition said in a post on X. Houthi attacks on civilian sites in the kingdom “will not go unpunished,” the spokesman, Turki Al-Malki, said.

The coalition said early Wednesday that it intercepted a ballistic missile north of Riyadh launched by the Houthis and later announced it had destroyed the launch platform used in the attack. The platform was in the Yemeni capital, Sanaa, and was being prepared for another strike on Saudi Arabia, the spokesman added.

The assaults on the Saudi airports follow a military campaign launched earlier this week by Yemen’s internationally recognized, Saudi-backed government to “eliminate” the Houthis, a group rooted in northern Yemen. The Yemeni armed forces claimed to have taken control of Red Sea areas.

UK Maritime Trade Operations said separately that a tanker was struck by projectiles off the coast of Qatar on Wednesday. It was the first reported strike on a tanker deep within the Persian Gulf in about a month.

The attack comes as tensions between Washington and Tehran heat up again. The White House has asked the Pentagon to draw up military options against Iran that could be executed before the US midterm elections, The Atlantic reported, citing two administration officials. Those backing the attack plan believe it could allow Trump to demonstrate strength and potentially declare some sort of victory ahead of the vote, it said.

The possibility of renewed US strikes on Iran helped push Brent crude up 1.1% to over $101 a barrel.

Houthi Threats

The Houthis, one of Tehran’s main proxy militant groups, took over Sanaa in 2014 and announced a blockade of Saudi ports, claiming the kingdom was besieging parts of Yemen.

Fighting picked up in early September, when the group started firing on Saudi Arabia almost daily and advanced south from their stronghold in northwest Yemen toward the Bab el-Mandeb, a crucial strait for energy tankers and container ships. That passage became even more vital after the Iran war endangered ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Houthi group’s missile threats originate from Sanaa as well as Saada and Amran in the country’s northwestern region, according to the Saudi-led coalition. GACA previously said Jazan and Najran airports were targeted in attacks on Monday, causing damage and injuring three people.

Pakistan has 48% of the poor in Greater Middle East; poverty in region remains at pre-pandemic levels

World Bank report says the region accounts for 14% of the world’s extreme poor, second only to Sub-Saharan Africa. The increase was driven by rise in poverty in Pakistan.

Debdutta Chakraborty

Facebook

Follow Us :

New Delhi: Pakistan is home to nearly half of the people living on less than $3 a day across the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan (MENAAP) region, the World Bank’s Economic Update on the region said Tuesday.

Pakistan accounts for 48 percent of the overall poverty in the region, the report says. This drove the regional increase, which is why MENAAP is the only world region where poverty remains above pre-pandemic levels and is still rising.

Three dollars is 830 Pakistani rupees and Rs 290. Pakistan’s poverty rate rose 6.4 percentage points at the $3.00 line and 3.2 points at the $4.20 line between 2018-19 and 2024-25 and exceeded 20 percent. Poverty rate is the ratio of the population whose income falls below the poverty line.

Show Full Article

Afghanistan, Syria and Yemen accounted for another 47 percent of the region’s population living below the same poverty threshold, according to the report .

Earlier in February, poverty in Pakistan surged to an 11-year high of 29 percent, while income inequality has reached its highest level in 27 years, according to the country’s official statistics.

The World Bank said the region accounted for 14 percent of the world’s extreme poor, second only to Sub-Saharan Africa.

“The increase was driven primarily by a rise in poverty in Pakistan,” the report said, noting that the country’s poverty rate increased by 6.4 percentage points at the $3-a-day line and by 3.2 percentage points at the $4.20 line between 2018-19 and 2024-25.

The bank attributed the deterioration to the Covid-19 pandemic, the devastating 2022 floods, a macroeconomic crisis characterised by high inflation and currency depreciation, and a prolonged period of economic adjustment that weakened real household incomes and employment opportunities.

The latest estimates show that poverty at the $3-a-day threshold has approached or exceeded 20 percent in Djibouti, Pakistan, Syria and Yemen.

The World Bank then projected Pakistan’s economy to grow 3.8 percent in the current fiscal year, while inflation is expected to reach 8.2 percent. However, once population growth is taken into account, real GDP per capita is projected to rise by only 2.2 percent, compared with 2.1 percent last year.

Also Read: Indians live 2.8 years longer than Pakistanis, says WHO. Here’s why

Shifts through the years
The 2024 World Bank update had projected 2.8 percent growth in FY25, 3.2 per cent in FY26, and inflation easing to 9 percent in FY26 for Pakistan and a current account deficit forecast at 0.7 percent of GDP in FY26. For 2025, the MENAAP report put Pakistan’s FY2025-26 growth at 2.6 percent and FY2026-27 at 3.4 percent. The bank has forecast a current account deficit of 0.8 percent of GDP and a fiscal deficit of 3.5 percent this fiscal year. Both are higher than the previous year, but remain within what the report described as manageable levels.

In 2025 the main threat was floods and weak agriculture. In 2026 it is the Gulf conflict, with fuel price jumps, a weaker current account, possible remittance losses, and El Niño exposure.

The World Bank said governments across the region were facing competing demands to protect households from rising prices while also responding to humanitarian needs arising from regional conflicts.

Fuel prices have risen sharply since the start of the West Asia conflict. Petrol prices increased by 40 per cent or more in Lebanon, Pakistan, Syria and the United Arab Emirates, while diesel prices rose by more than 40 per cent in Pakistan and the West Bank and Gaza.

According to the report, Pakistan sits in the “developing oil importers” group, which is projected to grow 4.3 percent in 2026, while the Gulf economies contract sharply.

Moreover, poorer households spend 35–50 percent of their budgets on food, so higher food and fuel prices hit them hardest. Pakistan is also among the countries where gasoline prices rose 40 percent or more, and diesel is up over 40 percent since the conflict began.

The increases were substantially higher in some other countries, with diesel prices rising by more than 80 percent in Lebanon and nearly 70 percent in the UAE.

Pakistan remains particularly vulnerable as an oil-importing economy. Along with Djibouti, Egypt, Jordan, Morocco and Tunisia, it faces the risk of higher inflation and commodity prices, reduced fiscal space, weaker remittance flows from Gulf economies and higher borrowing costs as geopolitical risks persist.

Pakistan’s inflation reached about 11 percent by midyear, according to the report. The fiscal-year forecast of 7.1 percent is however lower than the previous year, and the report projects it rising further to 8.2 percent in FY2027.

In fiscal and external position, Pakistan slips from a surplus to a growing deficit and is listed among the economies facing “significant debt or financing pressures”, alongside Algeria, Djibouti, Iraq, and Morocco.

The report notes that to counter it the government has introduced targeted fuel and farm assistance as it advocates for targeted cash transfers over broad subsidies as cheaper and better for fiscal space.

Then there are remittances. Pakistan is a major labour-sending economy to the Gulf. A prolonged slowdown in Gulf tourism, construction, and hospitality could weaken the income flowing home and remittance decline is named as a risk channel for oil importers generally.

The World Bank reclassified Pakistan, along with Afghanistan, from its South Asia region into a newly created grouping known as MENAAP — Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan in 2025.

Pakistan’s economic and external debt profile increasingly resembled that of MENA economies. Its debt-to-GDP ratio, estimated at around 33.4 percent, is broadly comparable with regional patterns in the region.

Pakistan also shares several demographic and labour-market characteristics with MENA countries, including a high youth dependency ratio, low employment-to-population rates and relatively weak labour-force participation. Female participation in the workforce remains particularly low, mirroring a broader challenge across much of the region.

Pakistan’s economic fortunes are increasingly connected to the Gulf and wider west Asia through remittances, capital flows and energy dependence. These ties have become an important component of Pakistan’s macroeconomic stability, outweighing the country’s relatively limited economic integration with other South Asian economies.

This is an updated version of the report.

items.title: Denmark plans ban on sharing AI deepfakes without consent
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Denmark's culture minister will on Thursday propose a bill to ban the digital copying and sharing of lifelike representations of a person, including their appearance and voice, in a bid to crack down on the spread of AI-generated deepfakes.
items.body:
Denmark's culture minister will on Thursday propose a bill to ban the digital copying and sharing of lifelike representations of a person, including their appearance and voice, in a bid to crack down on the spread of AI-generated deepfakes.
Culture Minister Zenia Stampe said in a statement that AI manipulated videos and images could lead to misinformation and create doubt about what is real
"One of the main goals of the bill is to get the tech giants to take down manipulated content quickly so that it causes as little harm as possible," she said
The bill is meant to protect both the wider public and artists, whose performances and work may not be imitated and subsequently shared
It does, however, include an exception for caricatures, parodies, satire and other work that criticises society and those in power
The proposal is still subject to parliamentary approval
Stampe said she hopes the bill will enter into force around the turn of year

items.title: US opens direct talks with Myanmar's generals, reversing years of isolation
items.author: CNA
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The Trump administration has begun direct talks with Myanmar’s military-installed government, according to US officials and others familiar with the outreach, in a sharp reversal of Washington’s efforts to isolate the country’s generals after the 2021 coup.The US Assistant Secretary of State

US opens direct talks with Myanmar's generals, reversing years of isolation

Michael Vance, nominee to be an Assistant Secretary of State for Intelligence and Research, participates in a US Senate Foreign Relations Committee nominations hearing in Washington, DC, US on Jun 18, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Elizabeth Frantz)

WASHINGTON: The Trump administration has begun direct talks with Myanmar’s military-installed government, according to US officials and others familiar with the outreach, in a sharp reversal of Washington’s efforts to isolate the country’s generals after the 2021 coup.
The US Assistant Secretary of State for Intelligence and Research, Michael Vance, played a leading role in the outreach, which has focused on shutting down scam centres that target Americans but could lead to broader engagement, including on Myanmar’s rare-earth mineral deposits, according to seven current and former officials and others familiar with the policy shift.
Vance joined talks with Myanmar leader Min Aung Hlaing in the capital Naypyidaw on Sep 15 and Sep 16. The meeting was aimed at securing the release of American businessman Adam Castillo but also provided an opening for further engagement, four of the people said.
Last month’s meeting - the highest‑level contact since the coup - underscores a broader Trump‑administration foreign policy tilt away from democracy promotion toward transactional engagement.

The presence of Vance, who was confirmed as the State Department’s top intelligence official in August, and his ongoing role in US policy toward Myanmar have not been previously reported.

Related:

IN FOCUS: 'I cannot go back' - Myanmar refugees fear repatriation as country gets cosier with Malaysia, Thailand

China charges 17 members of Myanmar-based human trafficking ring targeting Chinese citizens

MILITARY LEADER REMAINS UNDER US SANCTIONS Min Aung Hlaing, the former military chief, remains under US sanctions for human rights abuses, including the 2016-2017 mass killings and expulsions of hundreds of thousands of Rohingya Muslims that Washington declared a genocide. 
Less than two weeks after Vance’s visit, Myanmar’s military conducted an airstrike on a crowded marketplace in Rakhine state, killing over 50 people and injuring scores more, according to United Nations human rights officials.
The State Department said it engages with all groups in Myanmar on issues affecting US interests and raises the need to cease violence and release political prisoners.
“You don't solve problems by ignoring them. You solve problems by addressing them,” spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a statement.
A spokesperson for the military-backed government did not respond to a request for comment. Min Aung Hlaing, who has cited electoral fraud to justify the coup and labelled his opponents as terrorists, is seeking international legitimacy for his nominally civilian government.
Current and former officials say Vance has met players from all sides of Myanmar’s complex conflict and helped shape the Trump administration’s policy toward the country.
Intelligence chiefs - such as Vance - do not typically steer policy because of concerns about compromising analytic independence.
“If you let policy dictate to intelligence, you can't be sure you're getting a real honest assessment of the facts,” said Richard Betts, an adjunct senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations who has consulted for US intelligence agencies.
Pigott declined to address Vance’s role but said the administration “operates as a team with the president as the lead”.

Related:

Southeast Asia remains 'a clear priority' despite concerns over Trump tariffs: US envoy to ASEAN

A DETAINED AMERICAN, AND AN OPENING Castillo, a former head of the American Chamber of Commerce in Myanmar, was detained at Yangon airport on Jun 11 by Myanmar authorities on what his supporters have described as trumped-up charges. The US government has not commented on whether Castillo was wrongfully detained.
People familiar with the matter said White House, National Security Council and State Department officials held back-channel negotiations with Myanmar officials to secure his release. One person said Myanmar asked only "to have an official engagement at the right level with the US government" in return.
Castillo declined to comment beyond crediting President Donald Trump for his release.
The meeting builds on a June meeting between US and Myanmar officials in Tokyo also involving Vance, four people said. One of the people said officials from the Treasury Department, which oversees sanctions, the Department of Homeland Security, and the Pentagon took part.
It was unclear who represented Myanmar at the talks.
Vance, who became involved in Myanmar policy while advising Vice President JD Vance on Asian affairs, has also met in person and virtually with the democratic opposition and ethnic armed groups fighting the military, five of the people said.
A major focus of the US push is getting Myanmar's help in shuttering scam hubs operating on its territory that run romance and other frauds, which have scammed Americans out of billions of dollars. Two people familiar with the matter said the FBI has had direct contact with Myanmar’s authorities on cyber scams.
Researchers say many scams are run from areas under militia control, with some proceeds flowing to the military, raising doubts about whether Myanmar’s leaders are serious about enforcement.
US officials also discussed access to Myanmar’s massive deposits of heavy rare earths that are used in electric vehicles and wind turbines. US officials acknowledge obstacles: the deposits mainly lie in territory held by ethnic armies fighting Myanmar’s military government, and China, currently the main importer, could see any US role as a challenge.
Still, with Washington seeking to diversify supply chains away from China, Myanmar's deposits remain a recurring topic in conversations, the people said.

ASEAN's Five-Point Consensus

Following a 2021 military coup , the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) has excluded Myanmar from high-level meetings as it has yet to make meaningful progress on the bloc's Five-Point Consensus to end hostilities. 
During a meeting in April 2021, all ASEAN leaders reached a consensus about the situation in Myanmar.
The five points are:
First, there shall be immediate cessation of violence in Myanmar and all parties shall exercise utmost restraint.
Second, constructive dialogue among all parties concerned shall commence to seek a peaceful solution in the interests of the people.
Third, a special envoy of the ASEAN chair shall facilitate mediation of the dialogue process, with the assistance of the secretary-general of ASEAN.
Fourth, ASEAN shall provide humanitarian assistance through the AHA Centre.
Fifth, the special envoy and delegation shall visit Myanmar to meet with all parties concerned.

Collapse
Expand

FROM SANCTIONS TO ENGAGEMENT After the 2021 coup, President Joe Biden's administration froze Myanmar's assets at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and imposed sanctions on senior officers and military‑linked businesses.
In 2022, Congress authorised non-lethal support for the opposition, funding early-warning systems for airstrikes and incentives for officers to defect.
Most of those programs were cut during Trump’s foreign-aid overhaul last year, according to four current and former officials and State Department correspondence with Congress reviewed by Reuters.
The State Department said its engagement with the military government does not diminish its relationships with other groups. The US continues to provide assistance to areas outside military control, it said, without detailing that aid.
Rep. Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said the shift was “contrary to both our values and our interests”.
“By engaging Min Aung Hlaing while failing to implement congressionally mandated sanctions and deploy appropriated democracy funding, Secretary (Marco) Rubio is ceding US leadership and providing this murderous regime greater international legitimacy,” Meeks said in a statement to Reuters.
Myanmar's government, installed after elections criticised by rights groups as a sham, has hired lobbyists to press its case in Washington.
In April, Roger Stone, a longtime Trump adviser, began consulting for DCI Group on behalf of Myanmar's Ministry of Information, according to Foreign Agents Registration Act filings. Stone was convicted in 2019 of obstructing a congressional investigation into Russian interference in the 2016 election. Trump later pardoned him.
A newsletter distributed by DCI warned in June that Washington risked being shut out of access to critical minerals if it did not engage with Myanmar.
Myanmar leader Min Aung Hlaing is on a two-day visit to Malaysia as he looks for greater international legitimacy after being installed in April as civilian president.
